items.headline: High Court awards ministers Shanmugam and Tan See Leng S$230,000 each over Bloomberg article
items.summary: Justice Audrey Lim ruled on 14 July that Bloomberg and reporter Low De Wei defamed the two ministers in a December 2024 article on Good Class Bungalow deals, awarding each S$170,000 in general and S$60,000 in aggravated damages. Both ministers said they will donate the money to charity.

items.headline: Singapore economy grows 5.7% in the second quarter as AI-driven manufacturing leads
items.summary: MTI advance estimates released 14 July show GDP rose 5.7% year on year, above the 5.5% forecast but easing from the first quarter's 6.3%, with manufacturing up 12.2% on AI-related semiconductor demand. MTI kept its full-year growth forecast at 2.0 to 4.0% while flagging Middle East risks.

items.headline: Man who financed a WhatsApp and WeChat scam-account syndicate jailed four years
items.summary: Ronnie Low, 50, was sentenced on 14 July after pleading guilty to charges including membership of an organised crime group, and fined S$52,000. SIM cards seized from the syndicate, which sold anonymised chat accounts to scammers, were linked to 2,393 police reports and S$51 million in losses.

items.headline: Driver jailed five weeks after crashing a Porsche into Suntec City's Fountain of Wealth
items.summary: A 58-year-old Singaporean was sentenced to five weeks' jail and a 30-month driving ban after losing control of his Porsche and mounting the plaza, striking the landmark fountain. The court heard he had been driving without due care.

items.headline: India-UK free trade agreement takes effect, cutting tariffs on both sides
items.summary: The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement came into force on 15 July, giving Indian exporters duty-free access to about 99% of UK tariff lines including textiles and leather, while India phases out duties on UK whisky, cars, and machinery. India also secured a larger duty-free steel export quota.

items.headline: India's June merchandise trade deficit widens to a record $30.43 billion
items.summary: The goods trade gap hit $30.43 billion in June, against $19.12 billion a year earlier and a $26.5 billion forecast, the widest ever for the month. Imports jumped 31% to $70.84 billion on costly energy, while exports rose 15.5% to $40.4 billion, per Commerce Ministry data.

items.headline: RBI proposes easing rules for repeat large stake purchases in banks by funds
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India on 14 July proposed making it easier for asset managers, insurers, and pension funds to repeatedly acquire large stakes in Indian banks. The move is part of a wider push to draw capital and steady the rupee.

items.headline: India's inflation outlook clouded by renewed US-Iran tensions and an El Nino threat
items.summary: Economists warn that the spike in energy costs from the Gulf conflict, alongside forecasts of an emerging El Nino, could push India's inflation higher through the rest of 2026. The pressures complicate the RBI's room to support growth after June headline inflation breached its target.

items.headline: Starmer delivers an emotional final PMQs and wins a rare standing ovation from MPs
items.summary: In his 64th and last Prime Minister's Questions on 15 July, Keir Starmer told MPs this is the end of his political journey and pledged wholehearted support to successor Andy Burnham. Labour MPs gave him a standing ovation, drawing a reminder from Speaker Lindsay Hoyle that clapping breaks House rules.

items.headline: Incoming OBR chief Haskel warns the next prime minister against debt-funded spending
items.summary: Jonathan Haskel, nominated chair of the Office for Budget Responsibility and a former Bank of England rate-setter, told MPs on 15 July that the UK has little capacity for expansionary fiscal policy. He said debt-fuelled spending to boost growth would only push up inflation.

items.headline: Pound climbs to its highest against the euro in more than a year
items.summary: Sterling reached its strongest level versus the euro in over 12 months during 15 July trading, amid steadier UK political and inflation signals as Andy Burnham prepares to take office. Gilts and the FTSE 100 also featured in a busy session for UK markets.

items.headline: Burnham faces a day-one warning of a souring economy and oil-price risk
items.summary: The incoming prime minister has been warned he faces a worsening economy and the prospect of rising interest rates in his first six months, alongside a potential oil-price shock if the Iran war drags on. Internal forecasts have nudged fourth-quarter inflation up to 3.2%.

items.headline: Israeli air strike kills a family of three in central Gaza's Deir al-Balah
items.summary: An Israeli helicopter fired two missiles at an apartment near Al-Baraka roundabout on Wednesday, killing Omar Abu Qasem, 33, his wife Asma, 32, and their six-year-old daughter Habiba, while their three-year-old son survived. Israel's military said it targeted a Hamas fighter; more than 1,100 Palestinians have died since October's ceasefire.

items.headline: Russian strike on Odesa kills three as Ukraine hits Black Sea vessels
items.summary: A Russian missile struck a seven-storey Odesa apartment block on the fifth straight day of attacks, killing three and wounding several. Ukraine's drone force said it hit 17 Russian oil tankers, two gas tankers, and a tugboat, forcing a near-shutdown of the Sea of Azov.

items.headline: Update: US strikes Iranian-held Greater Tunb as Iran hits Gulf bases
items.summary: US Central Command said a 90-minute wave of precision strikes hit coastal-defence and cruise-missile sites on Iranian-occupied Greater Tunb Island to protect Hormuz shipping. Iran's IRGC retaliated overnight against Jordan's Prince Hassan Air Base, a US missile base in Kuwait, and facilities in Bahrain, and said it has no plans for negotiations.

items.headline: Trump hosts new Iraqi PM al-Zaidi and vows deals and a Basra-to-Ceyhan oil pipeline
items.summary: Trump welcomed Iraq's new prime minister Ali al-Zaidi to the White House, promising a lot of deals, while al-Zaidi said Iran-backed militias will have no justification to exist after 30 September. A pipeline deal with Chevron, TI Capital, and Qatar's UCC to carry about two million barrels a day is slated for signing Friday.

items.headline: OpenAI's first hardware device is reportedly a screenless, self-moving smart speaker
items.summary: OpenAI's debut consumer device will be a palm-to-tabletop, screen-free speaker with motorised moving parts, designed as an AI companion for the home, per Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. It is slated for release in 2027 and built around ChatGPT.

items.headline: ASML raises its 2026 sales forecast again and plans a 30% capacity expansion
items.summary: ASML lifted full-year 2026 net revenue guidance to 43 to 45 billion euros, up about 16% at the midpoint, and said it will boost production capacity by roughly 30% in each of the next two years on AI demand. Second-quarter revenue of 9.33 billion euros beat estimates.

items.headline: Nvidia ships a small number of H200 AI chips to China under a US license
items.summary: Commerce under secretary Jeffrey Kessler said a limited number of Nvidia H200 chips have now been shipped to Chinese customers after winning US approval, though he declined to name buyers or volumes. It is the first confirmed movement after months of stalled sales.

items.headline: Indian AI coding startup Emergent hits unicorn status with a $130 million Series C
items.summary: Emergent raised $130 million led by Creaegis at a $1.5 billion post-money valuation, a fivefold jump in six months, bringing total funding to $230 million. The app-building platform reports a $120 million revenue run-rate and more than 200,000 paying customers.

items.headline: OpenAI researcher Miles Wang in talks to launch a $2 billion AI drug-discovery startup
items.summary: Miles Wang is leaving OpenAI to start a company building AI models for drug discovery, reportedly raising about $200 million at a $2 billion valuation, with Lightspeed in talks to lead. Wang disputed the funding figures but did not give specifics.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley posts record second-quarter revenue as equities trading surges
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reported second-quarter revenue of $21.35 billion and profit of $5.58 billion, up 58%, with EPS of $3.46 against $2.94 expected. Equities-trading revenue hit a record $6.3 billion, roughly $1.9 billion above estimates, on the AI-fuelled global trading boom.

items.headline: PayPal draws a $53 billion joint takeover bid from Stripe and Advent
items.summary: Stripe and Advent International offered $60.50 per share, a roughly $53 billion bid backed by about $50 billion of committed bank financing and representing a 28% premium. PayPal shares jumped as much as 19% on the report.

items.headline: United Airlines beats on the second quarter and lifts its full-year profit forecast
items.summary: United reported adjusted second-quarter EPS of $1.99 against $1.88 expected, with revenue up 16% to $17.7 billion, and raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $9 to $11. It warned that higher oil could add nearly $6 billion to 2026 fuel costs, which rose 84% to $2.3 billion in the quarter.

items.headline: Traders ramp up July Fed rate-hike bets as Warsh calls inflation too high
items.summary: Market-implied odds of a quarter-point July hike climbed to about 50% from under 10% after June CPI, as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told Congress the data was one data point and not mission accomplished. NEC director Kevin Hassett countered that there is no excuse to raise rates now.

items.headline: 🎾 Wawrinka bows out of Gstaad for the last time, beaten by Faria
items.summary: The 41-year-old three-time Grand Slam champion, retiring at season's end, lost his final home-clay match 6-7(8), 6-4, 6-4 to Portugal's Jaime Faria. He hit 16 aces but went 0-for-6 on break points before an emotional on-court tribute.

items.headline: 🎾 Badosa routs fourth seed Kalinina to extend her win streak in Iasi
items.summary: Spain's Paula Badosa dropped just four games, beating fourth seed Anhelina Kalinina 6-3, 6-1 in the UniCredit Iasi Open first round for a sixth straight win. Kalinina served eight double faults in the match.

items.headline: 🏏 India eye a series clincher against England in the second ODI at Cardiff
items.summary: Leading 1-0 after a six-wicket win at Edgbaston, India can seal the three-match series at Sophia Gardens on 16 July. England, seeking to avoid defeat, recalled Brydon Carse after 13 losses in 19 ODIs since 2025.

items.headline: 🏎️ McLaren bring a new rear wing and the latest Mercedes engine to Spa
items.summary: McLaren confirmed a fresh rear wing and Mercedes' newest internal-combustion spec for Norris and Piastri at the Belgian Grand Prix. Technical chief Neil Houldey tempered expectations, pointing to a more significant upgrade package in Hungary the following week.

items.headline: 🏎️ Pirelli picks the C2, C3, and C4 tyres for a demanding Spa weekend
items.summary: For the Belgian Grand Prix on 17 to 19 July, Pirelli nominated the C2 hard, C3 medium, and C4 soft, giving drivers two hard, three medium, and eight soft sets. A mandatory two-compound race returns to consecutive compounds at F1's longest lap.

items.headline: Webb uncovers a hidden third giant planet in the famous Beta Pictoris system
items.summary: Astronomers found Beta Pictoris d, a gas giant at least about twice Jupiter's mass orbiting at roughly Neptune's distance on a 91-year path, 63 light-years away. It is the first directly imaged planet found chiefly via moderate-resolution spectroscopy, making Beta Pictoris only the second system with three directly imaged planets.

items.headline: An asteroid is unmasked as a 'dark comet' after its mysterious orbital drift
items.summary: Deep images from telescopes in Chile and Hawaii revealed a faint coma and a narrow tail more than 20 arcseconds long on a body previously catalogued as an asteroid. It is the first direct confirmation of cometary activity predicted from the object's anomalous, non-gravitational motion, tied to work by NASA JPL's Davide Farnocchia.

items.headline: Astronomers detect the first genuine sugar molecule floating in interstellar space
items.summary: A team led by Spain's Centre for Astrobiology detected erythrulose, a four-carbon sugar, in the molecular cloud G+0.693 near the Milky Way's centre using the Yebes 40m and IRAM 30m telescopes. It is the first true sugar found in space and can convert to threose, a possible RNA precursor.

items.headline: Four deep-sea technologies race to detect deadly earthquakes and tsunamis
items.summary: A Nature feature details how drilling ships, seafloor sensors, and repurposed undersea internet cables are being deployed to monitor subduction zones. Those zones are among the least-mapped places on Earth, with under 0.001% of the seafloor visually surveyed.

fun_fact.headline: Koalas have near-human fingerprints
fun_fact.body: Koalas have fingerprints so similar to a human's that even under a microscope forensic experts struggle to tell them apart, right down to the minutiae. As marsupials with no close primate relatives, koalas evolved the loops and whorls independently, a striking case of convergent evolution likely tied to gripping and stripping eucalyptus leaves.
fun_fact.source: PBS NOVA; Live Science (University of Adelaide research)

puzzle.title: The Mislabeled Jars
puzzle.body: Three sealed jars hold only apples, only oranges, or a mix. Each is labelled APPLES, ORANGES, or MIXED, but every label is wrong. Drawing one fruit from one jar, what is the fewest draws to label all three correctly?
puzzle.approach: Every label is wrong, so a single draw from the right jar cascades into all three.
puzzle.answer: One draw. Draw from the MIXED jar; being mislabelled it is pure, so its fruit names it. The ORANGES-labelled jar cannot be oranges or the just-found kind, so it is MIXED; the last is ORANGES.

word_puzzle.title: A-List
word_puzzle.body: Spelling Bee. Centre letter A (required); outer letters C, D, E, I, L, T. Make 4+ letter words using the centre A, letters repeatable; find the two seven-letter pangrams.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must use the centre letter A; two seven-letter words use all the letters.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangrams: DIALECT, CITADEL. Others include DILATE, DETAIL, DEDICATE, DELTA, IDEAL, TIDAL, CADET, CLEAT, DECAL, LACED, TACIT, ATTIC, LATTE, ELATED, LACTATE, TACTILE, CICADA.
